action: Slide the probe proximally from the current position.
interpretation: Observe the bone profile change from the smooth bone of the femoral shaft until it becomes more pointy and irregular.

action: Hold the probe stationary over the irregular bony prominence.
interpretation: Identify the pointy appearance as the greater trochanter.

action: Slide the transducer ventrally (anteriorly) while at the trochanter level.
interpretation: Visualize the small concavity on the anterior facet of the greater trochanter. Identify the structure within this concavity as the gluteus minimus tendon.

action: Maintain position on the anterior facet.
interpretation: Confirm this is the gluteus minimus in transverse view.

action: Slide the probe proximally and distally ('up and a little bit down') and adjust slightly laterally to scan the entire tendon.
interpretation: Observe for echogenicity changes or swelling. Specifically look for a large convexity of the tendon or an increase in cross-sectional area.

action: Focus attention on the bone surface underneath the tendon.
interpretation: Assess whether the bone surface is regular or irregular.

action: Rotate the transducer 90 degrees to obtain a longitudinal view of the gluteal tendon.
interpretation: Visualize the gluteus minimus in longitudinal view.
Trace the tendon transitioning into muscle tissue.

action: Slide back to the gluteus minimus and rotate the transducer back to the transverse view.
interpretation: Visualize the lateral facet of the greater trochanter (trochanter major).

action: Focus on the anatomy overlying the lateral facet.
Slide proximally over the gluteus medius.
interpretation: Note that the gluteus medius appears slightly more hyperechoic in this case.

action: Compare the echotexture with the previous finding.
interpretation: Recall that the gluteus minimus appeared slightly more hypoechoic.

action: Slide over the gluteus medius area.
Scan specifically to assess tendon morphology.
interpretation: Observe for changes in shape, such as increased or decreased tendon thickness.

action: Scrutinize the internal texture of the tendon.
interpretation: Check for changes in echogenicity and look for signs of full or partial ruptures.

action: Rotate the transducer to longitudinal view and slide proximally following the muscle.
interpretation: Follow the gluteus medius along its longitudinal axis.

action: Hold position at the proximal aspect.

interpretation: Visualize the tendon inserting onto the greater trochanter.
